dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: #Ah, you're here, {NICKNAME}. I sort of assumed that you didn't make it home very often.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: So, how are the travels going? Anything exciting happen lately? Your stories might be just the inspiration I need.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How do you like it here?

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: It's pretty good. Pleasant scenery, calm atmosphere... Good place to rest and rejuvenate your body and mind.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Sometimes, when I get sick of being in the Court of Fontaine, I get a strong urge to head off somewhere else for a while, and get a change of scenery. Somewhere without unruly customers, or tabloids spreading lies.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Oh yeah, loads. It was a long journey from Inazuma to Fontaine, after all.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: The wines and ballads of Mondstadt, the prosperous commercial hub that's Liyue Harbor, the bustling Grand Bazaar and the never-ending desert in Sumeru... I've seen it all.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: One thing I liked to do was head to the liveliest spot in town, find a seat, and just sit there people-watching all day. I wanted to get a sense of the local atmosphere, see the clothes people wore, imagine what kind of lives they lived...

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: I sometimes feel like to this day, most of the inspiration for my designs still comes from the things I saw back then on my travels... You of all people probably get what I'm talking about.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Hah, look at me — chat about anything for long enough, and I'll always find a way to make it about work.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Hmm... I guess it's a deeply ingrained habit of mine. I'm always on the lookout for inspiration, and every aspect of daily life is a potential source.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Anyway. Basically, I love traveling. Maybe one day, our travel plans will overlap and we'll bump into each other somewhere out there.

choices.text: Where would you like to go?

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Somewhere I've never been before. That's the only way I can find new inspiration.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: You know what, I've never been to Natlan or Snezhnaya... Hmm, maybe it's time to make some travel plans.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Every nation has a completely different fashion sense rooted in its unique culture. I have to keep incorporating new styles, adapting them, combining them, and innovating... That's the only way Chioriya Boutique can continue to stand at the forefront of fashion.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Would you like to have a chat with me?

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Huh, this one is for the books. A lot of people avoid chatting with me whenever they can help it, because they don't like what I have to say.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: The truth is, I just prefer it when people can cut to the chase and be straight with one another. The amount of effort some people put into beating around the bush and being diplomatic... It'd be so much quicker to just hash it out and be done with it.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: What about you? What's your preferred communication style?

choices.text: Direct and to the point, like you.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Excellent. That'll save us a lot of trouble.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: I remember one time when I saw a customer hesitating between two different colored outfits.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: I told her that she should pick the cream-colored one, since it went well with her hair and also accentuated her figure. She turned her nose up at that, and said that stains would show up more on the cream one than the gray one.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: So I said sure thing — if you're set on the gray one, I can make some adjustments so it'll look more stylish. But she didn't like that idea either, and she started saying that maybe the gray was a bit too dull.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: We went back and forth like that for a whole afternoon. In the end? She picked a red one...

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: I mean, I do understand where she was coming from. Her concerns were valid, it's just... People like that... they need to learn to prioritize between criteria when they're making a decision.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: If you want something that goes with your figure, pick the cream. If you want to get away with a few smudges and stains, pick the gray.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: But if what you really want is to stand out from the crowd so your crush will spot you as soon as they arrive at the party... then for goodness' sake, just tell me that as soon as you walk through my door!

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Phew... I'm getting all worked up just thinking about it. I need a moment to calm down...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Maybe she was just shy?

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: You're right. She was hesitant about telling me. But if she'd just been direct with me, we could have saved so much time, and then I would have been able to do a better job of tailoring her outfit to suit her needs.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Things like that happen all the time. It makes me all the more determined to never beat around the bush, and always be upfront and direct.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Sure, it might not have been the smartest approach. But for me at least, it's definitely the most efficient.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: All this is to say that I will never hide my true thoughts and feelings from you, and I'd like it if you could do the same for me.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Of course, if you ever find yourself compelled to say something like "Chioriya Boutique's outfits are hideous"... then I'd hope you at least follow it up with some sort of reasoned argument that I can consider.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: You don't seem like the type of person who'd say something just to be provocative. Unless... I dunno, you secretly enjoy the feeling of being thrown out of my front door, or something.

choices.text: I think sometimes, being tactful is better than being blunt...

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: You do? Well, I just find it a headache.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Maybe it's because I always have a clear and firm opinion on things. My feelings are never ambiguous — either I like something, or I don't.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Anything you want to do?

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Do you have any hagoita here? I could go for a round or two against you.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Hey, what's that look supposed to mean? Don't think I'm good for anything beyond sewing and stitching, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Nothing, just... Didn't know you were into that game. That's all.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: I played it all the time when I was growing up in Inazuma. I was actually one of the best players around.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: But no one knows how to play in Fontaine, and playing with beginners just feels... I don't know... kind of unfair to them?

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: You must have played it during your travels in Inazuma, right? I bet you're pretty good.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Well? You game? Don't tell me you're scared?

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Yeah, that's more like it! There's the Traveler everyone talks about.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Just so we're clear, I will definitely exercise my bragging rights if you lose.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: We can start whenever you're ready. I've got my own pair of hagoita that I can use.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: There's nothing in the rules that says you can't use two. I use twin blades in combat, what's so strange about using twin hagoita?

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: You can go ahead and use four hagoita against me, if you want. I don't mind.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Unless... you'd rather forfeit right now?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...I just hope you're not a sore loser!

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Oh, don't you worry about that. Even though the Chioriya brand is all about never admitting defeat, I have no problem with accepting a loss in a game between friends.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: On one condition, of course... You have to actually beat me first.

choices.text: What's the penalty for the person who loses?

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: Huh? Ooh, you wanna raise the stakes, do you? Fine by me, that'll make this much more fun.

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: If you lose... you come help out at my store for a few days. You can do some sweeping, organize the outfits, maybe do a little modeling...

response.speaker: Chiori
response.text: And if I lose, I help out at your place instead. It's up to you. I can sweep the place, or maybe do some decorating...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Good morning, Chiori.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Morning. I'm still waking up... Need to make myself some coffee.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Mind if I borrow your kitchen? I promise I'll clean up afterwards.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Good night, Chiori.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Another day, gone... How time flies.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: I'm gonna take another look at my pattern pieces. Go get some rest — no need to wait up for me.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: I haven't seen such a fine hot spring since before I left Inazuma... I've missed this.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: I got into the habit of taking a dip every day after work back when I still lived there. It's something I still enjoy... although in Fontaine, I'm limited to the humble bathtub in my home.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: I'm gonna go ahead and jump in. Is there anywhere to put my clothes? Or shall I just fold them up and leave them on the ground?

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: This was my favorite sight when I first moved to Fontaine. And now, it's one I get to see every day as I walk through the streets.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: Here, on these dazzling streets that seem to go on forever, the first corner of the Chiori fashion kingdom has been established.

dialogues.speaker: Chiori
dialogues.text: I will work hard to expand its territory over the coming years. In the meantime, you're always welcome to drop by for a visit.
